The high pressure pump is fitted on the left head and is controlled by the exhaust side camshaft by means of a three lobe cam which activates a pumping element inside the pump; the pumping element is activated three times for each revolution of the camshaft.

The high pressure pump has a diaphragm damper connected with the low pressure supply chamber to limit the supply duct impulses. The petrol vapours that are produced at this damper are collected in a special pipe which is later connected to the fuel return pipe to the tank.

1. Low pressure supply (6 bar)

2. High pressure supply

3. Fuel return to the tank

The diagram of the pump above highlights the contact points between the removable parts in red, the connection points with the metal seals or plastic deflectors in green and the location of the internal o-rings in blue.

The flow rate regulator, controlled by the control unit, which has the task of regulating the fuel high pressure, is located on the pressure pump. In particular, the needle for this regulator controls the closing of the (exhaust) port for the fuel from the high pressure chamber to the low pressure chamber for returning to the tank. To control the high pressure, the control unit closes the above mentioned port starting from a given distance of the pumping element stroke. In practice, if the port is left open for the entire duration of the pumping element stroke, the fuel is all sent to the supply circuit without an increase in the pressure in relation to the intake connected to the tank. If, on the other hand, the port is kept closed for the entire duration of the stroke, the pump is then working at maximum efficiency. For example, if the control unit decides to implement a 50% efficiency, it will control the closing of the exhaust port starting halfway along the pumping element stroke. If the regulator cannot be controlled by the control unit, the pump remains in the minimum efficiency position without producing a rise in pressure.

It can be deduced that in order to manage the fuel pressure, the engine management control unit needs to know the distance of the piston stroke in order to decide when to control the closing of the exhaust port. This information is obtained by the engine management control unit on the basis of the analysis of the top dead centre (rpm) signal for the crankshaft and the signal for the camshaft operating the pump.

The shut-off valve which intercepts the return flow of fuel to the tank is located on the fuel return pipe to the tank; this solenoid valve is only "open" with the engine started, whilst it is "closed" with the engine off or the ignition on. Its function is to prevent the draining of the high pressure pump to facilitate engine starting.

Fuel manifold (rail) for left cylinder head

It is connected to the pressure pump supply pipe and has a connector for connecting the rigid supply pipe to the right head rail. The maximum fuel pressure valve calibrated at 120 bar is also located on the rail.

The pressure pump supply pipe is connected, before reaching the pump, to the left rail by means of a spherical connector. In this way the pressure pump intake is in contact with a duct inside the rail, in turn connected to a chamber normally closed by the maximum pressure valve. When, for any reason, the maximum pressure valve intervenes (opens), the high pressure in the rail is discharged directly into the low pressure supply pipe for the pump by means of the connection mentioned above.

Throttle body for electronic accelerator system

Specifications

The throttle body includes the actuator, the throttle valve and the throttle position potentiometers (pontentiometers 1 and 2) incorporated in a single casing.

The actuator consists of a direct current motor with a dual stage gear that controls the position of the throttle valve thereby controlling the flow of engine intake air; the actuator works within a current range that determines the movement of the throttle from the minimum closing position to the maximum opening position; if there is a fault, the throttle valve returns to its lower mechanical stop position.

Accelerator pedal potentiometer

Specifications

The sensor consists of a casing secured to the accelerator pedal; the case contains an axially-located shaft connected to two potetiometers: a main one and one safety one.

A coil spring on the shaft ensures the correct amount of resistance to pressure while a second spring ensures return following release.

Operation

The accelerator pedal position is converted into an electrical voltage signal and sent to the control unit by the potentiometer connected to the pedal.

Fuel pump in the tank

There is a low pressure pump inside the fuel tank with a mechanical pressure regulator in parallel that allows the supply of the high pressure pump by means of a pipe. The supply pressure for the low pressure pump is 6 bar; the fuel return pipe from the high pressure pump recovery chamber also reaches the tank.

Specifications

The fuel pump is equipped with a permanent magnet electric motor that controls the pump and a terminal mount cover that contains the electrical and hydraulic connections.

The pump stage is single, peripheral flow type with high performance under low voltage and temperature conditions.

The advantages compared to pumps that operate on volumetric princples are that they are lighter and smaller.

Canister solenoid valve (petrol vapour flow)

The valve is used to regulate the flow of fuel vapours coming from the active charcoal filter by means of a signal received by the injection control unit.

Flow rate regulator

The flow rate regulator, fitted on the high pressure fuel pump, has the task of regulating the pump outlet flow rate on the basis of maps stored inthe control unit memory and the engine operating conditions; the wiring diagram showing the connection with the engine management control unit is illustrated below.

Specifications

Output voltage: 2V

Rest position: normally open (not controlled)

Operating pressure range: 6 – 120 bar

During the normal working cycle the closing of the regulator is operated by the control unit three times for every camshaft revolution.

Shut-off solenoid valve

Specifications

The solenoid valve is located on the fuel return pipe to the tank from the high pressure pump, in this way intercepting the return fuel flow to the tank; this solenoid valve is only "open" with the engine started, whilst it is "closed" with the engine off or the ignition on. Its function is to prevent the draining of the high pressure pump to facilitate engine starting.

High pressure injectors

Function

To ensure the injection of fuel into the cylinder in direct petrol injection systems.

Specifications

The injectors are the high pressure electromagetic type with a compact 2 pin connector and are connected directly to the injection manifold and spray directly into the combustion chamber. The opening time for the injectors and the quantity of fuel injected are managed by the electric control signal for the actual injectors; there is a wiring diagram below showing the connection with the engine management control unit; the injectors have the number of the cylinder to which they belong.

Maximum temperature at injector nozzle: <170°C

Electrical properties:

Peak current: 5,4 – 7,9

Peak time: 490 – 510 microseconds

Internal resistance: 0.8 Ohm

Function

To measure the pressure of the fuel in the rail, supplying the injection control unit with a feedback signal for regulating the pressure and the duration of the injection.

Specifications:

it is a piezoelectric pressure sensor, located on the right fuel rail, comprising a mixed metal and plastic casing. The metal part includes a diaphgram pressure meter; the plastic part contains the 3 pin connector; the wiring digram illustrating the connection with the engine management control unit is below.

Specifications:

Response time: 2 ms.

Supply voltage: 5 V

Supply current: 12 mA.

Signal:

Engine rpm sensor

Function:

to provide the engine managment control unit with the rotation speed and angular position signal for the crankshaft.

Specifications:

the sensor is the inductive type and comprises a casing with a metal coil and a 2 pin connector.

Operation

the changeover from full to empty determined by the presence or absence of a tooth for the flywheel fitted on the crankshaft brings about a magnetic flux change sufficient to generate an induced alternating voltage proportional to the number of teeth on the phonic wheel.

The frequency of the voltage sent to the electronic control unit provides it with the measurement of the crankshaft angular speed; the wiring diagram for the connection with the engine management control unit is illustrated below.

Positioning

the sensor is located on the right side of the crankcase, towards the flywheel: it is facing the flywheel on the crankshaft.

Camshaft timing sensors

Function:

To allow the engine management control unit to recognize which cylinder is at the end of the compression stroke.

Specifications:

The timing sensors are the Hall effect type, made up of a casign that contains a matching element and a 3 pin connector, a magnet and a signal acquisition circuit.

There are four sensors, one for each camshaft.

Positioning:

The timing sensors are located opposite the camshafts.

Detonation sensors

Specifications:

these are piezoelectrical type sensors fitted directly with a compact connector. There are two sensors, one on the right bank and one on the left bank. They measure the intensity of the vibrations produced by the mechanical pressure in the cylinders.

Positioning:

Sensor type: the sensor consists of an NTC thermistor

Oil pressure sensor

Specifications:

the oil pressure sensor is the linear type and is fitted on the oil filter mounting assembly.

Oil level and temperature sensor

Specifications:

The sensor controls the level and the temperature of the lubricant oil inside the oil sump fitted under the mono bloc.

This sensor is not connected to the engine management control unit but to a coupling which interfaces with the Instrument Panel Node (NQS).

Absolute pressure sensor

Specifications:

The sensor is located on the intake chamber and measures the pressure in the intake manifold; its function is to improve the engine carburation carried out by the control unit in fast shifts (sudden changes in engine speed and load conditions); it is basically considered, however, as a small refining implemented by the control unit in the above conditions calculated on the basis of the intake flow rate signal coming from the flow meter.
